Subject: One fully mature fictional historical English Toy Bulldog from the documented early twentieth-century Miniature Bulldog Club programme. Small but sturdy and compact, an original about8.5kg adult within the preferred under20lb class, with a developed broad deep chest, powerful shoulders, short strong back narrowing toward the loins and a gentle rise over the loin. Hindquarters lighter than forequarters. Large broad rather flat skull, broad deep stop, moderate facial wrinkles and short broad slightly upturned muzzle, projecting lower jaw with closed lips concealing teeth. Jet-black nose; two moderate wide-set dark eyes. Exactly TWO SMALL ROSE EARS: each small ear folds inward and BACKWARD onto itself, exposing the inner curved rose-like edge, with its short outer tip directed back from the face. Neither ear hangs forward over the cheek. Keep both ears low and modest against the broad skull; no upright French bat ears, triangular forward-flopping button ears or large pendant ear flaps. Short smooth close coat, fawn with modest white chest and small white toes, restrained dark muzzle shading; fawn is explicitly documented for Peter Pan, white chest visually observed, no precise colour derived from sepia. Short neck with moderate loose skin, ordinary sturdy short forelegs relative to hindlegs, developed hind joints and four complete ordinary grounded paws. One complete GENUINELY SHORT attached Bulldog tail, a small compact appendage emerging clearly from the rear rump and ending shortly beyond the rump, entirely below the back line. The short course gently points backward-downward and terminates in a plainly visible finite tip, its complete attachment and contour readable against the pale background. Do not extend it into a long tapering whip or add a long pointed strand. No measured tail length or docking/genetic origin is asserted. The own exact club standard specifies short tail belowback; no measured length, long extension, docked/naturallybobbed origin claim or modern parent-only anatomy. Adult Peter Pan standing photo supports developed frame/head/ordinary limb courses; its tail and farhind detail are obscured, so own norm complements them. No historical source pose or oval composition copied.

The COMPLETE VERY SHORT tail projects briefly LEFT from the rear rump, staying close to the rump and entirely belowback, with clear attachment, a compact continuous course and a distinct finite endpoint completely inside the frame. It remains visibly present rather than hidden, but must not become an elongated pointed tapering tail. Both small rose ears fold BACKWARD, with their inner curved edges exposed; neither tip falls forward as a button-ear flap. Keep all of both ears, eyes, head, body, four pawtips and tail inside frame with ample air above and clear ground below. profileEvidence.author: C
profileEvidence.summary: Historical Toy Bulldogs were affectionate, devoted companions with a keen interest in people and their surroundings. Food could coax them into obedience, and rabbits could stir their sporting interest. Their English club maintained a small show variety, later called the Miniature Bulldog.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Affectionate and attentive, historical Toy Bulldogs combined close companionship with an interest in outdoor sport.
